chunks: It is He who created the heavens and the earth with a definite purpose. The day He will say "Be," it will be. His word is the truth, His alone the power on the Day when the blast of the trumpet will be sounded. He knows the hidden and the visible. He is all-prudent and all-knowing.
ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of God mentioned in this verse regarding creation and the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the concept of *Kun Fayakun* as the instantaneous manifestation of divine will, affirming God's absolute sovereignty (*Al-Mulk*) over both the seen and unseen realms. It serves as a foundational proof for the Day of Resurrection (*Yawm al-Qiyamah*), linking the initial creation to the final judgment where the Trumpet is blown, thereby establishing God's omniscience and wisdom as the ultimate reality for believers.
